title: Mobile nail scope and state, council and registration boundaries
audience: Mobile nail technicians who offer manicure, pedicure, artificial nail and nail-art services at a client's location
learningOutcomes: Explain why cosmetic injectables and tattooing are outside this course
Identify which registration, licence or council classification may apply to a nail service in the state or council where the visit takes place
Decide whether a proposed nail service is on the approved service list before it is offered
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson are listed in officialReferences: Department of Health Victoria (registrable services and mobile exemption); Macedon Ranges Shire Council (council classification, Victoria); Northern Territory Government (registration covering artificial nails); WorkSafe Victoria (hazardous substances in the beauty industry).

instruction.heading: What is excluded from this course
instruction.body: Cosmetic injectables, including botulinum toxin and dermal fillers, are excluded from the mobile nail course, as they are from the mobile beauty course. Tattooing, semi-permanent make-up and body piercing are also outside this course. Whether a business offering those services needs a licence or is restricted depends on the state and council, and this course does not cover it. No lesson in this course gives authority to offer any excluded service. A client's request for an excluded service is declined on scope grounds and recorded.

instruction.heading: Registration and classification differ by place
instruction.body: Nail services are not treated the same way in every state and territory. In Victoria, the Department of Health lists beauty therapy among services that must register under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008. The registration is of premises and is handled through the council. The same Department page exempts mobile beauty therapists from registration, but the exemption does not extend to the principal place of business, and the position for mobile nail work specifically has not been confirmed for this course. Macedon Ranges Shire Council places nail services in its high-risk group, which needs periodic renewal and a fee. That classification belongs to one council and does not set the position for any other council. In the Northern Territory, the registration list includes artificial nails and manicures and pedicures, and the registration lasts one year. In other states and territories the position for mobile nail work has not been read for this course and is marked UNCONFIRMED in the sources. Before any nail service is added to the menu, check the list that applies at each location the business visits.

instruction.heading: Using the approved service list
instruction.body: The business keeps one approved service list. Each nail service on it has a short description, the products it uses, the steps it includes and the registration or classification it was checked against. A service that is not on the list is not offered, even if the technician has done it before or the client asks for it. Nail-art add-ons, extensions and removals are treated as separate entries when they involve different products, time or risk. The approved list is held in {{business:services.service_description}}. Each entry is reviewed when the products, the law or the council position changes.

procedure: Check the proposed service against the approved service list, and decline any item that is not on it
Confirm the service is not an injectable, tattoo, semi-permanent make-up or piercing, and decline it on scope grounds if it is
Identify the state, territory and council for the visit address
Check the registration, licence or council classification recorded for that location in the approved service list
Where the position is recorded as UNCONFIRMED, do not offer the service at that location until the business has confirmed it with the relevant authority
Record the scope check, the source and the date on the booking

workedExamples.situation: A client books a mobile manicure and asks the technician to apply a semi-permanent colour to her toenails and to add a small tattoo on the ankle.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the technician do, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: The tattoo is outside this course, and the technician must not offer it. Semi-permanent make-up and tattooing are excluded here, and the course does not state the position for them. The technician can offer the manicure or pedicure only if those services are on the approved list for that location. The request for the tattoo is recorded as declined on scope grounds, and the booking shows only the services that were confirmed.

workedExamples.situation: A technician whose business is registered in Victoria plans a mobile pedicure visit to a home in a council area that classes nail services as high-risk.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the registration of the business enough to start the visit?
workedExamples.reasoning: The Victorian registration position does not settle the council's own classification. The Macedon Ranges classification places nail services in the high-risk group, but that is one council only. The technician must check the classification for the council where the visit takes place, confirm the mobile position with the council or the Department, and record the council, the classification and the source. The visit does not go ahead on the Macedon Ranges position alone.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved service list, held with the booking system or in the kit
Safety data sheet for each product used at the visit
Record of the state, council and classification for each location the business visits
Gloves suitable for the products in use, as the product's safety data sheet directs

commonErrors.error: Adding a tattoo or semi-permanent make-up to the menu because the client asks for it.
commonErrors.prevention: These services are excluded from this course. Decline on scope grounds and record the decision.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a council's classification applies in every council.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the classification for the council where the visit takes place. Macedon Ranges is one council only.

commonErrors.error: Treating a mobile visit as outside the rules because it is at a home.
commonErrors.prevention: The Victorian exemption for mobile work has conditions and is not confirmed for nail work in this course. Check the position for the location before the visit.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Cosmetic injectables, tattooing, semi-permanent make-up and body piercing are excluded from this course. This lesson does not grant authority to offer any of them.

In Victoria, beauty therapy is listed by the Department of Health as a service that must register under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008 (page updated 22 May 2026). The mobile position for nail work is UNCONFIRMED for this course.
Macedon Ranges Shire Council places nail services in its high-risk group. This is one council's classification and may not apply elsewhere.
The Northern Territory registration list includes artificial nails. Registration is required where beauty therapy is offered for payment, and the page does not address mobile operators.
Completing this lesson does not register the business and does not authorise any nail service.

qualityStandard: Every nail service offered is on the approved service list, with a review date
No excluded service is offered, advertised or described as available under this course
The state, council and classification position for each location is recorded with the source and date
Any position recorded as UNCONFIRMED is not relied on until it is confirmed
documentationEvidence: Approved service list with review date
Scope check record for each location, with the source and date
Declined-request record for any excluded service
summary: Injectables, tattooing, semi-permanent make-up and piercing are excluded from this course
Registration and council classification for nail services differ by place
Each nail service must be on the approved list and checked for the location before it is offered
Completing this lesson does not register you or authorise any service

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks a mobile nail technician to add a small tattoo during a manicure visit. Under this course, what is the correct action?
options: Offer it at a higher price, since the technician is already on site
Decline it on scope grounds, because tattooing is excluded from this course
Offer it only where the client has signed a form on file

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about the Macedon Ranges classification of nail services is accurate?
options: It applies in every council in Victoria, so no local check is needed
It is council-specific and does not set the position for every council
It states that nail services are low-risk in every council area
